questions.q: If six-digit number $5x2y6z$ is divisible by $7, 11$ and $13$, then the value of $(x-y+3z)$ is?
questions.s:
The 'Pen-Free' Observation First: $7, 11, 13$ dekhte hi dimag ki batti jalni chahiye. Ye combined divisibility $1001$ ka specific pattern hai.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique / Exam Approach):
Dekh bhai TestRipper, is type ka ek fix pattern hota hai. Jo number in teeno se katega, wo essentially inke LCM ($1001$) se katega.
ConceptRule
7, 11, 13 Magic MultiplierAny 3-digit number $\times 1001$ becomes $ABCABC$

Toh $5x2$ aur $y6z$ bilkul judwa (identical) hone chahiye. Compare karlo: $y=5, x=6, z=2$.
Equation mein daalo: $x - y + 3z = 6 - 5 + 3(2) = 1 + 6 = 7$.

Method 2 (Concept Builder):
Number is form $1000 \times (5x2) + (y6z)$. $1001$ se divisibility ka matab hai alternate 3-digit blocks ka difference $0$ ya $1001$ ka multiple ho. Since it's a 6-digit number, difference exactly $0$ hi hoga.

Future Exam Takeaway: SSC me ab $1001$ ke alawa $7, 11, 13$ ka difference approach bhi puchte hain, par $ABCABC$ format sabse scoring hai.

questions.q: Find the number of proper divisors of $3^6 \times 5^4$.
questions.s:
Final Output: $34$

Core Conceptual Tool: Unitary Scaling.

Pen-Free Observation: Yaar yahan 'proper' divisors pucha hai, simple total nahi. Formula me end me bas number khud ko subtract karna hai.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique): Powers me $+1$ karke multiply kar, ye dega total. Proper pucha hai toh end me $1$ minus kar de.

Mathematically :-

$$ \text{Total Factors} = (6+1)(4+1) = 35 \\ \text{Proper Divisors} = 35 - 1 = 34 $$

Method 2 (Concept Builder): Proper divisor matlab wo number khud include nahi hoga uski counting me. Baki saara calculation total factors jaisa hi chalega.

Mathematically :-

$$ \text{Proper Divisors} = (p+1)(q+1) - 1 \text{ (Excluding } N \text{ itself)} $$

TCS Trap: Proper keyword miss karega to $35$ pehla option ya $B$ option me mil jayega and $-2.5$ leke aayega.

Exam Takeaway:

> Proper divisors = Total Factors $- 1$. Original number count nahi hota hai.

questions.q: Find the least common multiple of 1.2 and 2.7?
questions.s:
Answer is 10.8.

Pen-Free Observation: Decimals ka LCM nikalne me bache aksar fraction $12/10$ aur $27/10$ bana kar fans jate hain. Standard ninja technique lagao: decimal places equalize karo aur integers ki tarah treat karo.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique):
Numbers hain 1.2 and 2.7. Point bhool ja, 12 aur 27 treat kar.
LCM(12, 27): $27 \times 4 = 108$.
Ab original equation me ek decimal place tha, toh LCM me bhi wapas 1 decimal place laga de.
Final Output = 10.8. Khatam!

questions.q: What is the remainder when $(123456789101112\dots 444546)$ is divided by $16$?
questions.s:
Core Tool Triggered: Unitary Scaling (Tail Limit Observation)

Dekh bhai! Pura number dekh kar panic nahi hona hai, sirf base ki power pakad.

Pen-Free Observation: $16 = 2^4$, toh 16 ki divisibility check karne ke liye sirf number ki aakhiri 4 digits chahiye hote hain.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique):
Yeh counting series chal rahi hai $44, 45, 46$ tak. Toh last 4 digits hue $4546$.
Ab bas $4546 \div 16$ kar. $16 \times 284 = 4544$ hota hai.
Remainder kya bacha? 2 bacha. Options eliminate kar aur aage badh!

Future Exam Takeaway: Divisibility of $2^n$ depends entirely on the last $n$ digits. Aage ke saare digits sirf daraane ke liye hote hain.

questions.q: What is the ratio of the sum of the even factors to the sum of the odd factors of $240$?
questions.s:
Final Output: $30:1$

Core Conceptual Tool: Fixed Identities.

Pen-Free Observation: Ratio pucha hai toh samajh jao odd wale numbers bracket equation me apne aap even ke factor se cancel ho jayenge pura calculation mat karna.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique): Number ka factors tod de. Odd wale brackets ratio me upper aur lower dono side honge, cancel honge. Bas powers of 2 wale ka difference extract kar ratio ke liye.

Mathematically :-

$$ 240 = 2^4 \times 3 \times 5 \\ \text{Even component sum} = 2^1 + 2^2 + 2^3 + 2^4 = 30 \\ \text{Odd component sum} = 2^0 = 1 \\ \text{Ratio} = 30 : 1 $$

Method 2 (Concept Builder): Formula se karoge tab bhi $3, 5$ wale brackets same cancel hi honge fraction banate time.

Mathematically :-

$$ \frac{\text{Even Sum}}{\text{Odd Sum}} = \frac{(2^1+2^2+2^3+2^4)(3^0+3^1)(5^0+5^1)}{2^0(3^0+3^1)(5^0+5^1)} \\ = \frac{30}{1} $$

TCS Trap: Aadha dimag yahi ratio dono ki individual heavy values extract karne me nikal dega tabhi time kam padega exam me.

Exam Takeaway:

> Even to Odd factor sum ratio seedha only powers of $2$ component pe depend karta hai, baki primes ud jaate hain.

questions.q: In a parking lot, there are only two-wheelers and four-wheelers. The total number of vehicles is 60 and the total number of wheels is 200. How many two-wheelers are parked there?
questions.s:
Core Tool Triggered: JSM (Shift Method)

Dekh bhai... Linear equations $x$ aur $y$ wali equations banayega toh time nikal jayega. Shift method se bina pen chalaye solve kar.

Pen-Free Observation: Maan le parking lot mein sabke paas 4 pahiye hain.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique):
Toh total wheels $= 60 \times 4 = 240$ hone the. Lekin asal mein wheels sirf 200 hain.
Yeh 40 wheels jyada kyu aaye? Kyunki humne 2-wheelers ko bhi 4-wheeler ginn liya (matlab har 2-wheeler pe 2 extra pahiye assume kiye).
Extra wheels ko extra factor 2 se divide kar de: $40 / 2 = 20$. So, 20 two-wheelers the.

Future Exam Takeaway: Shift method avoids simultaneous equations completely. Shift all entities to the higher value and divide the error gap.

questions.q: The ratio between a two-digit number and the number obtained by reversing its digits is $4:7$. Find the ratio between the tens place digit and the units place digit.
questions.s:
Core Tool Triggered: Unitary Scaling

Dekh bhai, ye options se udane wala question hai! Pen uthane ki bhi zarurat nahi.

Pen-Free Observation: Number $ab$ aur reversed $ba$ ka ratio $4:7$ diya hai. Ratio $1$ se chota hai, matlab pehla digit dusre se chhota hoga. Option B aur D sidha eliminate ho gaye.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique - Option Elimination):
Option A: Ratio $1:2$ hai. Number maano $12$. Reverse hoga $21$. Seedha $\frac{12}{21} = \frac{4}{7}$ match kar gaya. Sirf 2 second ka game tha!

Method 2 (Concept Builder):
Let number be $10x+y$ and reverse be $10y+x$.
$\frac{10x+y}{10y+x} = \frac{4}{7} \implies 70x + 7y = 40y + 4x \implies 66x = 33y \implies \frac{x}{y} = \frac{1}{2}$.

Future Exam Takeaway: Ratio of digits pooche toh sidha base values assume karke fraction check kar lena, equation banane mein time waste mat karna.

questions.q: If $n = 8^{12}$, then how many perfect squares are there in its factors?
questions.s:
Final Output: $19$

Core Conceptual Tool: Fixed Identities.

Pen-Free Observation: Perfect square matlb factors me numbers ki powers hamesha even (multiple of 2) chalengi. Pehle prime base convert maro.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique): Given base $8$ ko pure prime base $2$ me change kar. Uske baad jo bhi exponent bane usko 2 se divide maar kar ek 1 add kar de zero power ke liye.

Mathematically :-

$$ 8^{12} = 2^{36} \\ \text{Even powers} = \{0, 2, 4 \dots 36\} \\ \text{Count} = \frac{36}{2} + 1 = 19 $$

Method 2 (Concept Builder): Square hone ka matlab hai prime factor ka exponent $2k$ ki form me express hona chahiye.

Mathematically :-

$$ N = P^{2k} \\ \text{Squares factor count} = \left\lfloor \frac{2k}{2} \right\rfloor + 1 $$

TCS Trap: Baccha division $36/2$ kar leta hai par zero exponent count (jaise $2^0 = 1$ is also perfect square) krna bhool kar seedha 18 tick maar aayega.

Exam Takeaway:

> Perfect squares in factors nikalne ki trick hai: $(\text{Highest even exponent} / 2) + 1$.

questions.q: Find the highest power of 10 in $50! + 60! + 70!$?
questions.s:
The 'Pen-Free' Observation First:
Bhai jab addition ho raha ho (multiply nahi), toh common zeroes bahar nikali jaati hain. Iska matlab addition mein total zeroes hamesha wahi decide karega jo sabse choti term ($50!$) hogi!

Method 1 (Ninja Technique / Exam Approach):
Sabse choti term = $50!$. Hum sirf iske trailing zeroes nikalenge. (Zeroes 5 ki power pe depend karte hain kyunki 2 ki power already bohot zyada hoti hai).
Successive division of 50 by 5:
$\frac{50}{5} = 10$
$\frac{10}{5} = 2$
Inko add kar do: $10 + 2 = 12$.
Toh 50! mein end mein 12 zeroes aayengi, toh combined sum mein bhi 12 hi rahengi.

questions.q: Find the maximum power of 3 in 60!
questions.s:
Core Tool Triggered: Successive Change (Legendre's Formula)

Dekh bhai... Factorials mein prime powers nikalne ka universally fastest tareeqa lagana hai.

Pen-Free Observation: Divisors ko baar baar 3 se divide kar aur quotients ko add kar.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique):
60 ko 3 se divide kar: quotient 20.
Phir 20 ko 3 se kar: quotient 6.
Phir 6 ko 3 se kar: quotient 2.
Bas in quotients ko add kar de: $20 + 6 + 2 = 28$. Is hack se kabhi calculation error nahi aayega!

Future Exam Takeaway: Don't rely on complex summation notations; just successively divide the quotient by the prime and add the results.

questions.q: If $N = 3^{14} + 3^{13} - 12$, What is the largest prime factor of N?
questions.s:
Core Tool Triggered: Unitary Scaling (Algebraic Factorization)

Dekh bhai aise karna hai... Jab constants aur powers mix hon, toh factors isolate karke algebra laga.

Pen-Free Observation: 12 extract karke format ko square identities jaisa banaya ja sakta hai.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique):
Common le pehle. $N = 3^{13}(3 + 1) - 12 = 4 \times 3^{13} - 12$.
12 common le le: $12(3^{12} - 1)$.
Ab $3^{12} - 1$ ko algebra se tod $(3^6 - 1)(3^6 + 1)$. $3^6$ hota hai 729.
Bracket ho gaye $728 \times 730$.
Factors break kar: $728 = 8 \times 7 \times 13$, aur $730 = 10 \times 73$.
Maximum bound prime factor perfectly 73 nikal gaya!

Future Exam Takeaway: Extract common constants to reveal standard $a^n - b^n$ algebraic identities. The largest prime is always hidden inside the factored brackets.

questions.q: What is the remainder when $2^{736}$ is divided by 117?
questions.s:
The 'Pen-Free' Observation First:
117 thoda bada number hai, toh CRT (Chinese Remainder Theorem) ka socho. Options me se us number ko check karo jo 117 ke coprime factors ko set kare.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique / Exam Approach):
Dekh bhai TestRipper, 117 ko tod de $13 \times 9$ me.
Mod 9: $2^3 = 8 \equiv -1 \implies (2^3)^{245} \times 2 \implies (-1)^{245} \times 2 = -2 \equiv 7 \pmod 9$.
Options dekh, $16 \pmod 9 = 7$ de raha hai. Baaki options (1, 32, 64) nahi de rahe. Seedha Option 16 tick kar aur aage badh!

Method 2 (Concept Builder):
Proper check karne ke liye 13 se bhi verify kar le. $2^6 = 64 \equiv -1 \pmod{13}$. Toh $2^{736} = (2^6)^{122} \times 2^4 \implies (-1)^{122} \times 16 \equiv 16 \equiv 3 \pmod{13}$. Option 16 isko bhi satisfy karta hai.

Future Exam Takeaway:
Bade divisors ko hamesha co-prime factors me tod kar options eliminate kiya karo, mazdoori time kill karti hai.

questions.q: Find no. of zeroes in $[100!]$?
questions.s:
The 'Pen-Free' Observation First: Factorial me Zeros nikalne hain, yani number of $5$s check karne hain. $100$ tak ki range me ye ek standard data hai jo yaad hona chahiye.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique / Exam Approach):
Dekh bhai, $100!$ ki sidhi calculation Legendre's Formula se nikalti hai. Hum successive division karte hain $5$ se.
$\frac{100}{5} = 20$.
$\frac{20}{5} = 4$.
Ab $4$, $5$ se chota ho gaya toh wahi ruk ja. Dono ko jod de: $20 + 4 = 24$. Option D answer!

Method 2 (Concept Builder):
The formula is $\lfloor \frac{100}{5} \rfloor + \lfloor \frac{100}{5^2} \rfloor + \lfloor \frac{100}{5^3} \rfloor \dots$
It counts one $5$ from every multiple of 5, then a second $5$ from every multiple of $25$.

Future Exam Takeaway: $100!$ ka 24 zeroes hota hai ye directly yaad rakho, bahut baari badi values ke base calculations me use hota hai.

questions.q: What is the remainder when $2^{3^{51}}$ is divided by 17?
questions.s:
The 'Pen-Free' Observation First: Divisor 17 prime hai aur base 2 uske coprime hai. Matlab Fermat bhai ki entry hogi! Power $3^{51}$ bohot badi hai, usko Fermat divisor pe break karna padega.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique / Exam Approach):
Fermat ka rule: $2^{16} \equiv 1 \pmod{17}$. Matlab base 2 ki power ko 16 ke remainder cycle me lana hai.
Toh step 2 hai power $3^{51}$ ko 16 se bhag de: $3^{51} \pmod{16}$.
$3^2 = 9, 3^3 = 27 \equiv 11, 3^4 = 81 \equiv 1 \pmod{16}$.
Cyclicity 4 ki aayi. Power 51 ko 4 se bhag de, remainder 3 bachega. Yaani $3^{51} \equiv 3^3 \equiv 27 \equiv 11 \pmod{16}$.
Akhiri step: Base ki actual effective power 11 ban gayi! Humein ab sirf $2^{11} \pmod{17}$ nikalna hai.
$2^4 = 16 \equiv -1 \pmod{17}$.
$2^{11} = (2^4)^2 \times 2^3 \equiv (-1)^2 \times 8 \equiv 1 \times 8 = 8$. Final answer 8 aaya!

Method 2 (Concept Builder):
The tower power concept relies on Euler's Totient function. $\phi(17) = 16$. So you first reduce the tower power modulo 16, then apply the result back to base modulo 17.

Future Exam Takeaway: Tower powers dekhte hi top ki power ko base divisor ke totient function ($\phi$) se mod karo.

questions.q: What is the result when the sum of the digits of $(10^{15} + 1)$ is divided by $11$?
questions.s:
Core Tool Triggered: Unitary Scaling

Dekh bhai aise karna hai... language ka ghatiya trap samajh.

Pen-Free Observation: Sawaal me dhokha hai! Sawaal number ko $11$ se divide karne ka nahi hai, uske 'Sum of digits' ko $11$ se divide karne ka hai.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique / Exam Approach): $10^{15} + 1$ number dikhne me kaisa hoga? Ek $1$, uske beech me $14$ zeros, aur aakhiri me ek $1$. Is pure number ke digits ko jodega toh sum aayega $1 + 0 + \dots + 1 = 2$. Ab $2$ ko $11$ se divide karega toh Remainder $2$ hi aayega na mere bhai!

Method 2 (Concept Builder): $10^n + 1$ form me sum of digits hamesha $2$ hi hota hai, chahe $n$ kuch bhi ho.

Future Exam Takeaway: Language ko dhyan se padho. 'Sum of digits' aur 'Number' me confuse mat hona.

questions.q: Raj wants to type first 200 natural numbers. Find out the number of times he has to press the keys.
questions.s:
Answer is 492.

Pen-Free Observation: Typewriter/keystroke ke sawaal range segmentation se hote hain. 1-digit, 2-digit aur 3-digit ke bundles alag-alag count kar.

SegmentCalculation
1 to 99 numbers $\times 1 = 9$ keys
10 to 9990 numbers $\times 2 = 180$ keys
100 to 200101 numbers $\times 3 = 303$ keys

Takeaway: Direct leap karo, sum it up: $9 + 180 + 303 = 492$ keystrokes.

questions.q: Find the greatest possible 5-digit number of the form $4a3b2$ which is divisible by $36$.
questions.s:
The 'Pen-Free' Observation First:
'Greatest' pucha hai matlab hum digits ko $9$ se check karna shuru karenge. Divisibility $36$ yani $4$ and $9$ dono lagana hai.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique / Exam Approach):
Number is $4a3b2$. For divisibility by $4$, last two digits '$b2$' must be divisible.
To maximize, test largest $b$: $b=9 \implies 92$ is div by $4$. So $b=9$ set kar do.
Now number is $4a392$. For divisibility by $9$, digital sum must be div by $9$.
Sum $= 4 + a + 3 + 9 + 2 = 18 + a$.
To maximize, put $a=9 \implies 18+9 = 27$ (div by $9$).
So the greatest number is $49392$.

Method 2 (Concept Builder):
Pehle hamesha choti constraint wala rule lagao (jaise $4$ ke liye bas last $2$ digits). Phir global rule (jaise $9$ ke liye sabka sum) apply karo.

Future Exam Takeaway:
Maximization ke questions me variable ko default $9$ assume karke condition check kiya karo, speed $2x$ ho jayegi.

questions.q: Find the remainder when $20^{23}$ is divided by 23.
questions.s:
The 'Pen-Free' Observation First: Power aur divisor ko dekh! Divisor 23 ek prime number hai aur power bhi prime 23 hi hai. Seedha Fermat's theorem chamakna chahiye.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique / Exam Approach):
Ye Fermat's Little Theorem ka dusra advance roop hai.
Basic form: $a^{P-1} \equiv 1 \pmod P$.
Advance form: $a^P \equiv a \pmod P$.
Yahan prime $P = 23$ diya hai. Toh sidha $20^{23} \equiv 20 \pmod{23}$. Dekhte hi answer 20 mark kar de bhai!

Method 2 (Concept Builder):
Agar Fermat's base version apply karna ho toh: $20^{22} \equiv 1 \pmod{23}$. Both sides 20 multiply kar, toh $20^{23} \equiv 20 \pmod{23}$ ban jayega.

Future Exam Takeaway: Divisor agar Prime ho, toh powers break karne me Fermat's Rule hi Divisibility ka raja hai.

questions.q: What is the remainder when $1^1 + 2^2 + 3^3 + \dots + 10^{10}$ is divided by 4?
questions.s:
The 'Pen-Free' Observation First:
Options 0, 1, 2, 3 hain. 4 se division check karna hai. Even bases ka power $>1$ hai toh vo seedha 4 ka multiple ban jayenge (Remainder 0). Sirf odd bases calculate karne hain!

Method 1 (Ninja Technique / Exam Approach):
Dekh bhai TestRipper, $2^2, 4^4, 6^6, 8^8, 10^{10}$ sabme 4 chupa hai, toh inka remainder sidha 0 bachega. Ab odd bases pe Mod 4 lagao:
$1^1 \implies 1$
$3^3 = 27 \implies 3$
$5^5 \equiv 1^5 \implies 1$
$7^7 \equiv (-1)^7 \implies -1 \equiv 3$
$9^9 \equiv 1^9 \implies 1$
Sum = $1 + 3 + 1 + 3 + 1 = 9$. Final step: $9 \pmod 4 = 1$.

Method 2 (Concept Builder):
Bhai, divisibility ki property hai ki sum ke andar har term ko individually divide karke remainder nikal sakte hain. Odd terms alternating 1 aur 3 remainder dete hain mod 4 me, cyclicity follow hoti hai. Aisa breakdown karo questions ka, SSC CGL first attempt me nikal jayega.

Future Exam Takeaway:
Jab 4 se bhag ho aur even base power $\ge 2$ ho, toh usko direct kaat ke 0 likh dena, mazdoori mat karna!

questions.q: Find the remainder when $2^{100}$ is divided by $102$.
questions.s:
The 'Pen-Free' Observation First:
Base $2$ aur Divisor $102$ coprime nahi hain. Iska matlab direct totient nahi lagega, pehle 'Cancellation Rule' lagana padega!

Method 1 (Ninja Technique / Exam Approach):
Expression: $\frac{2^{100}}{102} = \frac{2 \times 2^{99}}{2 \times 51}$. Upar niche $2$ se cancel kar do. Nayi form: $\frac{2^{99}}{51}$.
Euler's Totient $\phi(51) = 51 \times \left(1 - \frac{1}{3}\right) \times \left(1 - \frac{1}{17}\right) = 32$.
Power reduce: $99 \pmod{32} = 3$.
Remainder of $\frac{2^3}{51} = \frac{8}{51}$ is $8$.
Crucial Step: Jis $2$ se pehle kata tha, usko wapis multiply karo! $8 \times 2 = 16$.

Method 2 (Concept Builder):
Agar $\text{HCF}(a, n) > 1$ ho, toh Euler ya Fermat fail ho jate hain. Pehle common factor HCF cancel karke coprime banao, solve karo, aur end me HCF se wapas multiply karo.

Future Exam Takeaway:
SSC CGL Mains me cancellation rule ka ye trap bohot common hai. Cancellation factor ko side me likh liya karo taaki end me bhool na jao.

questions.q: Which of the following numbers is completely divisible by 99?
questions.s:
The 'Pen-Free' Observation First:
99 matlab usme 9 aur 11 dono ki divisibility lagegi. Sabse pehle 9 ka digital sum check karke ghatiya options udane hain.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique / Exam Approach):
Dekh bhai, 114345 ka digital sum dekh: $1+1+4+3+4+5 = 18$ (9 ka multiple hai).
Ab 11 ka check kar isme: alternate sum le. $S_1 = 1+4+4 = 9, S_2 = 1+3+5 = 9$. Difference = $9-9 = 0$.
Ye number dono shartein poori kar raha hai, yahi correct hai.

Method 2 (Concept Builder):
Options ki scan aise kiya kar: $135792 \implies$ sum 27 (divisible by 9). But 11 rule: $(1+5+9)-(3+7+2) = 15-12 = 3$ (not div by 11). Direct elimination.

Future Exam Takeaway:
99 ki divisibility check me C9 (casting out nines) first pass hona chahiye, aur bache options me hi 11 ka rule lagao.

questions.q: Find the rightmost two non-zero digits of $30^{2720}$.
questions.s:
Core Conceptual Tool: Value Putting & Symmetry.

Pen-Free Observation: Trailing zeroes kisi number form me extra multiple limits add karti hain. Pura Zero block hi ignore maro matrix separation property lagake.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique): Zero nikal bahar kar de 10 multiple split lagake. Baaki sirf $3$ bachega base. 3 ke upar power exact $4$ ki multiplier sequence me fit baith rhi hai matlab 81 banayegi series ko 'X1' solve ke lie.

Mathematically :-

$$ 30^{2720} = (3 \times 10)^{2720} = 3^{2720} \times 10^{2720} \\ \text{Ignore zeroes part} \to 3^{2720} \\ 3^{2720} = (3^4)^{680} = 81^{680} \\ \text{Unit} = 1 \text{, Tens} = (8 \times 0) = 0 \implies 01 $$

Method 2 (Concept Builder): Exact cyclical behavior and modular inverse scaling on core number parts.

Mathematically :-

$$ \phi(100) = 40 \\ 3^{40k} \equiv 1 \pmod{100} \\ 2720 \pmod{40} = 0 \implies \text{Last two are } 01 $$

TCS Trap: Yahan decimal zeros aur extra zeros add hone ki confusion lagakar numbers $10^{X}$ ko directly mix karke powers calculate karne mat baitho.

Exam Takeaway:

> Trailing zeroes check limits me core non zero base separate mark karo, aur remaining portion power cyclicity rules execute karo.

questions.q: When a number is divided by $65$, the remainder is $31$. When the same number is divided by $13$, the remainder is?
questions.s:
Core Conceptual Tool: Fixed Identities.

Pen-Free Observation: Pehla divisor $65$, exactly dusre divisor $13$ ka multiple $(13 \times 5)$ hai. Seedha purane remainder pe strike maar.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique): Jo pura remainder hai (31) usi ko naya divisor (13) maanke seedha operation complete kar de.

Mathematically :-

$$ 65 \pmod{13} == 0 \text{ (Condition passed)} \\ 31 \pmod{13} \implies 31 - (13 \times 2) = 31 - 26 = 5 $$

Method 2 (Concept Builder): By Division Lemma algorithm, $N = 65k + 31$. Extract $13$ completely.

Mathematically :-

$$ N = 13(5k) + 13(2) + 5 \\ N = 13(5k+2) + 5 \implies \text{Remainder is } 5 $$

TCS Trap: TCS pehla divisor multiple nahi rakhega (like $D_1=65$, $D_2=14$), us case me operation invalid hota hai answer "Cannot be determined" ayega.

Exam Takeaway:

> Rule constraint: Agar pehla divisor dusre se perfect divide hota hai to final Remainder sidha $R_1 \pmod{D_2}$ hota hai.

questions.q: If $x = 0.535353\dots$ and $y = 0.424242\dots$, then what is the value of $(x+y)$ as a fraction?
questions.s:
The 'Pen-Free' Observation First:
Bar bar recurring digit hamesha fraction me denominator '9' lati hai. In dono ki periodicity same hai, toh direct sum kar sakte hain.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique / Exam Approach):
Dekh bhai, $0.\overline{53} = \frac{53}{99}$. Dusra $0.\overline{42} = \frac{42}{99}$.
Dono ka base common hai, seedha numerator jod de: $\frac{53+42}{99} = \frac{95}{99}$.
Ye sawal literally 2 second ka tha.

Method 2 (Concept Builder):
Mixed recurring me dhyaan rakhna, agar $0.2\overline{53}$ hota toh $\frac{253-2}{990}$ likhna padta. Lekin yaha direct pure recurring decimal diya tha.

Future Exam Takeaway:
Pure recurring fractions (digits repeat from the start) me directly numbers add/subtract kiye ja sakte hain bina fractions banaye ($0.53 + 0.42 = 0.95$ recurring).
